Last week, after Apple released Xcode 27.1 beta 1, Bitrig immediately added support for building and testing iPhone Duo applications, and equipped it with an interactive 3D simulator, allowing developers to freely fold, tilt, rotate and place the device. Details are as follows.

Bitrig now lets users personally operate a 3D iPhone Duo

Bitrig originally launched as a simple vibe-coding application, allowing users to generate native SwiftUI applications directly within the Bitrig main app on iPhone via text or voice prompts.

Since then, the platform has expanded significantly, adding Mac applications that let users use the full Xcode development toolchain, built-in iPhone simulator, on-device testing, and export projects to Xcode or distribute applications via TestFlight and the App Store.

Last Friday, after Apple released Xcode 27.1 beta 1 supporting the building and testing of iPhone Duo applications, Bitrig also immediately launched its own iPhone Duo support, presenting the simulator in a more interactive way.

The following is Bitrig co-founder and CEO Kyle Macomber explaining the features brought by this update:

Try various postures. The iPhone Duo can lie flat on a desk like a laptop, or stand on a bedside table like a screen. Whether open, closed, or half-folded, placed vertically or horizontally, your application needs to adapt. Bitrig's 3D simulator lets you pick up, fold, and flip the device, and observe the application's response in real time. Respond with the hinge. Use onHingeChange to detect the state when the phone is folded, thereby driving various interactions and effects, similar to Apple's "unfold effect," making the outer screen feel like a window to the inner screen. Read hinge data in real time when opening and closing the device in the built-in simulator. Create a hands-free experience. Use ArrangementView to arrange media content in the upper half and control options in the lower half, convenient for use when the iPhone Duo is lying flat on a desk. Support landscape display, allowing users to use your application on the outer screen when the device is standing on its side. Use both screens simultaneously. Add CameraCaptureAccessory to the outer screen to provide useful visual content for the person facing the camera.

Macomber also mentioned: "Bitrig helps you manage multiple versions of Xcode. You can start preparing applications for iPhone Duo with the beta version first, then switch back to Xcode 27 at any time to build and release updates."
